title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Term-End Window for Renewal Remittances
content:
### Term-end window

The term-end window of a renewal remittance the insured makes on an NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) policy (tiers without ICC coverage) is measured from the day of the remittance to the term end. It is:

1. **30 days** when the premium booked at the expiring term's start was paid in full by payments other than escrow disbursements;
2. **15 days** when escrow disbursements paid any of it;
3. **no days** otherwise.

When the remittance falls outside the window, the remittance before the credits booked with it may not be less than the renewal premium.

"The premium booked at the expiring term's start" is the premium charged for that term at new business or at renewal; the payments counted are those applied to the expiring term.

| Payments applied to the expiring term | Window | Inside when the remittance is |
|---|---|---|
| Non-escrow payments covering the whole premium booked at the term start | 30 days | 30 days or fewer before the term end |
| Any escrow disbursement among them | 15 days | 15 days or fewer before the term end |
| Neither | No days | On the term end itself |

*Hypothetical case.* A term whose start premium the insured paid in full by check: a remittance 20 days before the term end is inside the window. Had the lender's escrow paid part of it, the window would be 15 days and the same remittance would be outside it.
